name: Palace
label: Drag City
lede: Will Oldham started as a teenage movie actor in Louisville, cut country records with Slint members and his own brothers under a new band name almost every time, and wrote a song Johnny Cash ended up singing.

eras.title: The boy preacher who shot Slint
eras.text: Before Palace, Will Oldham was a Louisville kid who'd acted for John Sayles and hung around the punk scene, close enough to Slint to take their most famous photo. By 1992 he was playing open mics under joke names and cutting a first single for a new Chicago label, Drag City.

years.h: At 17, Will Oldham is a boy preacher in Matewan
years.p: Louisville's Will Oldham plays Danny Radnor in John Sayles' film about the 1920 West Virginia coal war.
years.xp: Acting came first and never stopped. Oldham kept taking film roles for decades, from Sayles' Thousand Pieces of Gold to Kelly Reichardt's Old Joy.

years.cap: The Spiderland cover, shot by Will Oldham
years.h: Oldham shoots Slint treading water for the Spiderland cover
years.p: The photo of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] in a Kentucky quarry that fronts Spiderland is Will Oldham's. Three of the heads above the waterline will soon play on Palace records.
years.xp: [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]], [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]] and [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] all turn up on early Palace sessions. The Louisville circle was small, and the same few people kept swapping instruments.

years.h: Grant's Tomb, Birdie Num Nums and a Derby party as Wing It
years.p: Before Palace has a name, Will Oldham and friends play open mics in Bloomington, Indiana and Louisville under whichever joke name is handy.

years.h: The first Palace Brothers single, on a brand-new label
years.p: Drag City issues Ohio River Boat Song backed with Drinking Woman, a 7-inch for a Chicago label that is barely out of the box.

eras.title: Whoever's in the room
eras.text: The first Palace records were old-time country played by Louisville post-rock musicians who barely knew the idiom, and that was the point. Oldham recorded with Slint members in a shared house, then with his brothers at their parents' place, and toured Europe before most of America had heard him.

years.h: Royal Trux talk Drag City into signing Will Oldham
years.p: According to Stereogum, [[Neil Hagerty|dabacddd-26f0-45b9-b6eb-17fa31af7329]] and [[Jennifer Herrema|4e505aec-707e-49b3-a2f3-b8c6513549e2]] pushed the label to sign him, then produced the Palace Brothers single Come In under the name Adam and Eve.

years.h: Palace Brothers open for Big Star on the night Big Star reunite
years.p: The first listed show is April 25 at the University of Missouri in Columbia, opening for [[Big Star|21d177ba-3d51-461e-9b3f-ad9a80b419dc]] and Alex Chilton.

years.h: There Is No-One What Will Take Care of You, country played by Slint
years.p: Britt Walford and Brian McMahan of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] back Will Oldham, with [[Todd Brashear|9fecf563-bce8-4960-89e9-7075bbffe84f]] on lap steel and Grant Barger on organ. The one cover is Washington Phillips' I Had a Good Mother and Father.
years.xp:
The musicians swapped guitar, bass and drums between songs, which is why the record wobbles like a front-porch session. The Toronto Star called it quietly beautiful and slightly askew.

Mojo later put it in The Mojo Collection: The Greatest Albums of All Time (2001).
play: There Is No-One What Will Take Care of You
I Had a Good Mother and Father

years.h: Three nights at Lounge Ax with Silver Jews, Smog and Pavement
years.p: Palace plays Drag City's July 29-31 Invitational in Chicago, on bills with [[Silver Jews|1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983]], [[Smog|89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34]] and [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]].

years.cap: Flyer for Palace Brothers at the Cas.Rock, Edinburgh, October 31, 1993
years.h: Palace Brothers cross Ireland, Britain and Germany, billed as ex-Slint
years.p: Todd Brashear, Britt Walford and Brian McMahan make up the band for a tour of Ireland, the UK, the Netherlands and Germany.
years.xp:
Royal Stable lists Dublin's Baggot Inn on October 24, Edinburgh's Cas.Rock on October 31 and London's Garage on November 6, with dates running to mid-November.

The Edinburgh flyer prints "featuring ex-members of Slint" under the name, and notes the Palace Brothers LP is out on Big Cat.

years.h: Oldham records Horses in Bob Nastanovich's house
years.p: The third Palace single is cut in a house Will Oldham shares with [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]] and Britt Walford. Horses is a Sally Timms and Jon Langford song Oldham had sung for years; [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] overdubs guitar.
years.xp: Brian McMahan played drums, Walford bass and Brashear lap steel. The B-side, Stable Will, came from sessions in an abandoned Louisville building with the Pale Horse Riders, and was mostly written by Bryan Rich under the name Roy Black.

years.h: Mid-July to early August on Lollapalooza
years.p: Per the fan database Royal Stable, Palace spends the 1994 tour season on Lollapalooza dates across North America.

yt: Live at Thread Waxing Space, NYC, June 24, 1994
years.h: Will Oldham alone with a cassette deck, and no title
years.p: He makes the second Palace Brothers album almost solo on a Marantz cassette recorder bought from Bryan Rich, mostly at his parents' house in Louisville. It ships untitled.
years.xp:
More sessions happened at brother [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]]'s house in Birmingham, Alabama; Ned plays bass and Paul Oldham percussion on one track. The name Days in the Wake came later.

AllMusic's Mark Deming called it the simplest record in the Palace canon, and among the best.
play: You Will Miss Me When I Burn

years.h: Palace Songs aim for gratitude on the Hope EP
years.p: Hope is meant as a turn toward thanks after Days in the Wake. It's cut at Chicago's Acme with [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] on keys, plus London sessions with [[Sean O'Hagan|62b38d85-b2b9-4c59-8b86-9336c6e58491]], and includes a Leonard Cohen cover.

years.h: The Palace Revue and Motor Show ends on Elvis covers
years.p: A Midwest tour with a name like a county fair wraps at Cicero's in St. Louis on November 23.

eras.title: A new name for every band
eras.text: Palace Brothers became Palace Songs, then Palace Music, then just Will Oldham, because the line-up kept changing and Oldham thought the name should too. Steve Albini recorded two of the records that made the reputation.

years.big: "...so that people would be aware of the differences."
q: the same group of people playing on it
years.h: Why every Palace record has a different name on it
years.p: Will Oldham says he wanted listeners to notice the band had changed. So Palace Brothers became Palace Songs, then Palace Music, then just Palace.
years.xp:
The full line, as Wikipedia prints it: "I thought it was important to call it something different so that people would be aware of the differences." The cast rotated from record to record, so the name did too.

By 1997 he was releasing under his own name, and a year later as Bonnie "Prince" Billy.

years.h: Viva Last Blues is the loud one, with Steve Albini behind the desk
years.p: Cut in Alabama, it has Bryan Rich on lead guitar, [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]] on bass, [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] on keys and [[Sebadoh|d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f]]'s [[Jason Loewenstein|d06bfcfa-7be5-40ca-82be-4c7d3bdb44c3]] on drums.
years.xp:
NME and Spin both gave it 8/10. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 60 on its list of the top 100 albums of the 1990s.

John Green gave New Partner four stars on The Anthropocene Reviewed in 2019.

yt: Live at Hollywood Alley, Mesa AZ, November 16, 1996
years.h: Albini, David Grubbs and a drum machine with a band credit
years.p: At Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota, [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] plays piano and organ on Arise Therefore, and a Mayatone drum machine is credited as a member named "Maya Tone".
years.xp: Alternative Press gave it five out of five. Mojo called it a phantom creation beyond the comprehension of even its creator.

years.h: Palace retires, and Joya carries only Will Oldham's name
years.p: No band name on the cover this time.

years.h: Drag City collects the Palace 7-inches on Lost Blues and Other Songs
years.p: The scattered singles come together on one album, starting with Ohio River Boat Song.

eras.title: Bonnie "Prince" Billy and the Man in Black
eras.text: From 1998 Oldham worked as Bonnie "Prince" Billy, and the Palace songs found singers far bigger than him. He kept acting too, from Kelly Reichardt's Old Joy to a Kanye West video.

years.h: Nat King Cole, Billy the Kid and a new stage name
years.p: Will Oldham starts working as Bonnie "Prince" Billy, a name that mixes Bonnie Prince Charlie, Nat King Cole and Billy the Kid (William Bonney).
years.xp:
Oldham said "Bonnie Prince Charlie has such a beautiful ring to it", and only later noticed that Billy the Kid was William Bonney.

The point of a pseudonym, he said, is to let the audience and the performer have a relationship that is "valid and unbreakable."

years.cap: Will Oldham as Bonnie "Prince" Billy, Marseille, March 27, 2001
years.h: The first Bonnie "Prince" Billy album is the one critics reach for first
years.p: I See a Darkness is Will Oldham's first record under the new name.

years.h: Johnny Cash sings I See a Darkness for American III
years.p: Cash records Will Oldham's song for American III: Solitary Man, with Oldham on backing vocals.

years.cap: Will Oldham (left) on stage with Little Wings, December 2004
years.h: Oldham joins the Silver Jews on Tanglewood Numbers
years.p: Will Oldham sings on the 2005 album with [[David Berman|bbed0b05-cf87-45e6-aee8-259b34077969]], [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] and [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]], twelve years after the Drag City Invitational bill they shared.

years.h: Oldham plays Kurt, the drifter, in Kelly Reichardt's Old Joy
years.p: Kurt takes an old friend on a camping trip in the Oregon woods.

years.h: Oldham and Zach Galifianakis lip-sync Kanye West on a farm
years.p: The alternate video for Can't Tell Me Nothing is Will Oldham and Zach Galifianakis on a farm, mouthing the words.
